findings.summary: FileSyncStrategy is a thin adapter that delegates entirely to IFileSyncOrchestrator.sync() and only reshapes the return type. It adds no behavior, validation, or translation beyond mapping FileSyncResult fields to WorkResult fields and returning null on no-changes. Given that IWorkStrategy has only one implementation, this is ceremony wrapping with minimal value.
evidence: src/sync/file-sync-strategy.ts:16-52 - FileSyncStrategy wraps IFileSyncOrchestrator with identical parameters and only reshapes the return value
findings.suggestion: If no second IWorkStrategy implementation is planned, consider inlining the orchestrator call directly in SyncWorkflow or having FileSyncOrchestrator implement IWorkStrategy itself. If a second strategy is planned, this is fine as-is.

findings.summary: RepositoryProcessor's constructor accepts an optional components bag with 10 injectable dependencies. While DI is correct, the bag is so wide that it functions as a poor-man's DI container. The class itself is a thin facade that only creates a FileSyncStrategy and delegates to SyncWorkflow, making the 10-dependency constructor disproportionate to its behavior.
evidence: src/sync/repository-processor.ts:42-56 - Constructor takes gitOpsFactory, log, and a components bag with 10 optional fields
src/sync/repository-processor.ts:118-134 - The process() method is 4 lines: create strategy, resolve defaults, delegate to syncWorkflow
findings.suggestion: Consider a builder or a dedicated composition root function that constructs SyncWorkflow directly, removing the need for RepositoryProcessor to hold 10 dependencies when it only uses 2 (syncWorkflow, fileSyncOrchestrator). The wide bag pattern is test-friendly but the class itself is a thin pass-through.

findings.summary: createPR() and mergePR() in pr-creator.ts are standalone functions that internally instantiate PRWorkflowExecutor and call getPRStrategy. They act as a procedural layer on top of the existing IPRStrategy + PRWorkflowExecutor OOP layer. PRMergeHandler calls these functions rather than using the strategy directly, creating an unnecessary intermediary.
evidence: src/vcs/pr-creator.ts:146-186 - createPR() instantiates getPRStrategy and PRWorkflowExecutor internally
src/sync/pr-merge-handler.ts:24-37 - PRMergeHandler.createAndMerge calls createPR() free function, repacking its own parameters into PROptions
findings.suggestion: Inject IPRStrategy into PRMergeHandler directly instead of going through the procedural createPR/mergePR functions. This would remove one level of indirection and make the dependency explicit.

findings.summary: RepoIterationContext in sync-command.ts bundles 12 fields into a single object passed to processSingleRepo and its sub-functions. While this avoids 15+ function parameters, the context bag has grown wide enough that each sub-function destructures a different subset. This is a minor cohesion concern but not severe since it is scoped to the CLI entry point.
evidence: src/cli/sync-command.ts:306-400 - processSingleRepo uses subset of ctx fields, passes different subsets to sub-functions
findings.suggestion: This is acceptable at a CLI composition root. If it continues to grow, consider splitting into phase-specific contexts (lifecycle phase context, sync phase context, settings phase context).
